claims.statement: TVI-CAMS is an internal multi-tenant TESDA compliance working layer for TVI schools running TWSP/CFSP scholarship batches; TESDA's SIS, T2MIS, and BSRS remain the authoritative systems, the tool never holds official standing, and UI copy must never imply official approval or submission.

The initial tenants are the three schools AKB, J3ED, and NEN (scoped by Supabase RLS), roles are Admin/Coordinator/Trainer/Viewer, programs TWSP and CFSP are stored as configurable records rather than hard-coded branches, and the stack is a single Next.js 16 App Router app (React 19, TypeScript strict, Tailwind v4, Supabase Postgres+Storage, Clerk, pnpm) with no separate backend requiring Node 22+.

The doc read order is README.md → CONTEXT.md → CLAUDE.md → RULES.md: CLAUDE.md explains the architecture and the why, RULES.md is the non-negotiable checklist to read before any code change, and where the two appear to disagree RULES.md wins and the drift should be fixed.

RLS is the security boundary and UI hiding is usability only — every authorization decision is made by Postgres RLS via app_private.* helper functions (RULES §1.1), and a JS-side tenant filter is a bug even when it returns the right answer because it signals the query was written assuming no RLS (RULES §1.2).

Import direction is app → modules → shared → lib/supabase and is lint-enforced via import/no-restricted-paths in eslint.config.mjs (RULES §2): raw database.types.ts rows are importable only by module data/ layers, shared/ must never import modules/ or app/, and another module's data/ is private — import its domain/ or ui/ instead.

No statement may be executed against the live Supabase project without explicit user permission (RULES §10, [deny] via .claude/settings.json permissions.deny): the rule covers execute_sql including read-only selects, apply_migration, branch create/merge/reset, and edge-function deploys by any route (MCP, CLI, psql), because there is one hosted project and no staging, so an unreviewed statement lands on real tenant data; schema questions are answered from the checked-in migrations and database.types.ts first.

assets/, preview/, screenshots/, ui_kits/, and uploads/ are do-not-edit design handoff directories (RULES §6): they are ported verbatim from the design bundle, excluded from lint/build via globalIgnores in eslint.config.mjs, and a PreToolUse hook (.claude/hooks/protect-static-dirs.sh) blocks edits there.

The verification loop is pnpm lint (ESLint flat config enforcing the import boundaries), pnpm test (Vitest run over tests/unit/ covering mappers and module domain/ layers with fixed as-of dates; Node 22+ is required because Vitest 4's rolldown crashes at startup on older Node), pnpm exec tsc --noEmit (strict typecheck, no dedicated script), and pnpm test:e2e (Playwright over e2e/ booting pnpm dev, signing in with Clerk test keys pk_test_*/sk_test_* only per .env.example); RLS/tenant-isolation tests, when they exist, run against real Supabase with no mocks and the real-Supabase integration suite is still outstanding.

Per the 2026-09-10 catalog verification (issue #230, re-verified via pg_proc/pg_policies), the per-version state of the checked-in migrations is: 20260906114735 (the ADR-006 school registry + platform admin) is applied and now recorded — its file was renamed from 20260906130000 so the filename matches the recorded version, with all ten of its policies plus app_private.is_platform_admin() verified present; 20260904120000 (the user-admin write policies) is applied by hand but NOT recorded in the migration table, so /users/new's admin-grant path is no longer RLS-denied; 20260906120000 (the ensure_profile_tenant_membership RPC) is genuinely missing — the one real gap, since modules/auth/data/provisioning.ts calls it; 20260910120000 (the ADR-001 billing domain: seven tables, the billing_type enum, new batches/learners/program_billing_rules columns, RLS policies, and the compliance-evidence storage DELETE policy) is still pending and is omitted from both in-repo ledgers (docs/DATA_MODEL.md and supabase/migrations/README.md); and the 20260831120000 dev operational fixture now lives in supabase/seeds/ (nothing in that directory runs automatically — [db.seed] points at a placeholder seed.sql), with its rows already present in the single hosted project.

The evidence upload I/O in modules/documents/data/evidence.ts (the private compliance-evidence bucket, signed-URL reads) is written but not exercised: two dashboard toggles (Clerk's Supabase integration and Supabase Third-Party Auth) are still unset under issue #122, so every call fails with an RLS denial indistinguishable from a code defect, and the file must not be debugged against a live project until #122 is closed.

The blocker-gate family (blockingDocuments, blockerCount, blockingDocumentNames) in modules/documents/domain/compliance.ts implements ADR-004 D4 and is unit-tested in tests/unit/doc-blockers.test.ts, but no screen or other code consumes it — it is a ready public domain surface, not live screen behavior.

After any migration the agent must regenerate lib/supabase/database.types.ts and then update the affected mappers and domain types (RULES §3.20); new migrations are additive with 20260528160300 canonical, and docs/DATA_MODEL.md's applied/pending ledger must be updated in the same PR with the status moved to applied only after the migration has actually run.

The live database has drifted from the checked-in repo (issue #230, verified 2026-09-10) and is ahead of its own records rather than behind: objects exist that the migration table does not know about — the by-hand-applied 20260904120000 user-admin write policies, and an orphan public.tenants policy ('Tenants selectable by Clerk user') that no checked-in migration defines and that omits the is_active check its reviewed counterpart enforces. The one real gap is public.ensure_profile_tenant_membership (20260906120000), absent on the live project even though modules/auth/data/provisioning.ts calls it. Because neither the supabase/migrations/ directory listing nor list_migrations alone is authoritative, objects must be verified by name (pg_proc for functions, pg_policies for policies), and #230 must be reconciled (including what to do with the dev-fixture rows already in the hosted project) before assuming a clean db push.

Per the records the live Supabase schema is 18 tables, 36 foreign keys, and seven enums, while the checked-in target is 25 tables, 52 foreign keys, and eight enums once the pending migrations land: the eighth migration (20260910120000) adds the seven tables program_modules, scholarship_cost_schedule, learner_identities, attendance_records, batch_trainer_assignments, billing_records, and tenant_settings with 16 new foreign keys and the billing_type enum, and is the only pending migration that changes shape.

The ADR-006 /schools/new write path creates a tenant plus its registered programs atomically: the Server Action composes the validated SchoolCommand (pure rules in modules/tenancy/domain/schoolDraft.ts) and the write goes through modules/tenancy/data/schools.ts's createSchool, which calls the security invoker public.create_school RPC on the Clerk-scoped anon client (never the service-role client), so RLS still evaluates every statement inside the transaction; the screen is gated on the platform-admin axis via the current_user_is_platform_admin() RPC snapshot (getPlatformAdminSnapshot), deliberately not on resolveRouteRole or tenant role, and results distinguish created / duplicate-code / denied (RLS 42501) / sync-failed / unconfigured.

Platform admin is a separate axis from profile_role, not a fifth role value: it is its own public.platform_admins table (RLS enabled with no policies, so it is unreadable and unwritable through the Clerk-scoped anon client and the role cannot be self-granted), resolved in-app only through the security definer public.current_user_is_platform_admin() boolean. Its reach is the school registry only — tenants, qualifications, tenant_qualifications, unassigned profiles, and seating a tenant's first member (whose INSERT policy carries two load-bearing guards: it cannot seat itself, and only into a memberless tenant) — with no policy granting any compliance table (batches, learners, documents, lamr_*, activity_log); granting one is a boundary change that needs its own ADR (RULES §7, ADR-006 P3).

The Vitest unit suite (pnpm test, include pattern tests/unit/**/*.test.ts in vitest.config.mts) now spans 21 spec files in tests/unit/, including school-draft.test.ts, user-access.test.ts, sidebar.test.ts, sign-in-verification.test.ts, and tenant-access.test.ts.
